Mr. Mukul Singh Dangi, Advocate for the appellant.
2.
Mr. Deepak Bisht, Deputy A.G. with Mr. Bhaskar Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant/convict would submit that by the impugned judgment/order dated 29.10.2022 F.T.S.C./Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun in Special Sessions Trial No.168 of 2021 the appellant/convict has been convicted under Sections 376, 504, 506 of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years along with fine of ` 20,000/- u/s 376 IPC, one year's R.I. u/s 504 IPC and further one year's R.I. u/s 506 of IPC.
4. Learned counsel would further submit that the appellant/convict was on bail during trial and he has never misused the liberty of bail granted to him.

5. He would further submit that the appellant/convict has been wrongly convicted by the trial court as there is no evidence against the applicant/convict of any sexual assault upon the body of the prosecutrix/victim; that, the alleged incident took place on 11.07.2021 while the FIR was lodged on 15.08.2021 i.e. after one month of the alleged incident and there is no explanation for that delay by the prosecution.
6.
Learned State Counsel would vehemently oppose the bail application but would admit that the FIR is delayed by one month and there is no sufficient explanation for such delay.

7. Having considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties but without expressing any opinion about the final merits of the case, in the opinion of this Court, the appellant/convict deserves to be enlarged on bail during the pendency of present criminal appeal.
Let the appellant/convict be released on furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the amount of  60,000/- and personal bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court concerned.
